prompts.name: statefulset-for-redis
prompts.prompt: I need to deploy a Redis cluster as a StatefulSet in ConfigHub with 3 replicas and persistent storage. The Redis pods should use the redis:7.2 image and listen on port 6379. Set it up in my redis-prod Space.
prompts.expected_output: Authors literal StatefulSet plus required headless Service/PVC-template resources with security, probes, requests/limits, and exact namespace/storage questions. Because unresolved namespace/storage choices and multiple resources materially affect scope, asks those focused questions before Bash. Once answered and explicitly requested, maps one resource per Unit, submits one exact literal Unit create at a time to the host permission system, verifies each, and hands eventual delivery to a separate release-publish step.

prompts.name: lock-down-namespace-networking
prompts.prompt: I want to lock down networking in my app namespace. Default deny everything, then allow my frontend pods to talk to backend pods on port 8080, and backend to reach the database on port 5432. All pods need DNS. How do I set this up in ConfigHub?
prompts.expected_output: Authors explicit ingress/egress NetworkPolicies including namespace DNS, validates selectors/namespaces/IP-family assumptions, and explains default-deny consequences. Produces one-resource-per-Unit proposals and a staged proof plan; does not apply or create resources.

prompts.name: cronjob-with-rbac
prompts.prompt: I need a CronJob that runs every hour to clean up expired sessions from our database. It needs a ServiceAccount with permission to read Secrets (just the one named db-credentials) and ConfigMaps. The cleanup script is in our image at ghcr.io/myorg/session-cleanup:v2.1.0. Put it in the myapp-prod Space.
prompts.expected_output: Resolves the missing namespace and exact resource/Unit names before acting. Authors separate ServiceAccount, Role, RoleBinding, and CronJob resources with least privilege/resourceNames for db-credentials, sensible concurrency/history/security settings, and external-secret cautions. Uses the exact image and one resource per Unit. Once the required details and literal source file are bound, submits exactly the first scoped `cub unit create` call through the host permission system, verifies it read-only, and treats each remaining create as a separate next step; an explicit external-overlay stop produces zero Bash calls.
